high_consensus.description: Real operational gap: the SDD defines rollout but not failure recovery. Rollback paths for FR-1/FR-2 are highly actionable and reduce production risk with moderate documentation effort.
Excellent and necessary. FR-2 regression testing is currently subjective; adding measurable equivalence criteria makes validation repeatable, auditable, and automatable.
Critical blocker-level item. The document itself flags this as unverified; unresolved API syntax uncertainty can invalidate FR-7 implementation. Must be resolved or mitigated before final sign-off.
Strong improvement with clear ROI. Replacing manual-only checks with at least a CI smoke harness materially improves reliability and repeatability, though it adds moderate implementation effort.
Good domain-specific concern. Boundary conditions between generated constraints and path-scoped rule files are a real source of drift/overwrite bugs and should be explicitly defined.

disputed.description: High-value consistency/security fix. It identifies a concrete contradiction in stated policy versus configuration; either justified exception or scoped restriction is required.

blockers.concern: FR-7 compliance hook is fail-open on errors and missing state, creating an easy bypass path
blockers.why_matters: Any JSON parse error, missing file, or hook runtime failure silently allows App Zone writes, undermining the core compliance control and making policy enforcement unreliable.
blockers.location: Section 2.7: Agent-Based Compliance Hook (Fail-open design, Performance constraint)
blockers.recommendation: Use fail-closed for high-risk paths (App Zone), add explicit degraded-mode behavior, and require structured error telemetry plus operator override rather than automatic allow.

blockers.concern: Forked context quality equivalence is judged subjectively, without measurable acceptance criteria
blockers.why_matters: Comparing to the 'most recent unforked execution' is noisy and non-deterministic; silent quality degradation in PRD/SDD/sprint artifacts may go undetected.
blockers.recommendation: Define objective quality rubrics and regression metrics (required sections, coverage checks, defect rates), then automate before/after scoring.

blockers.concern: Heavy reliance on manual validation for core behavior changes introduces regression risk
blockers.why_matters: FR-1, FR-2, FR-4, and FR-5 depend mostly on manual checks, which are not repeatable and will miss edge-case regressions in permissions, context isolation, and rule loading.
blockers.recommendation: Add automated integration tests for skill invocation, tool permission enforcement, fork behavior, and path-rule activation; gate merges on these tests.

blockers.concern: Tool restrictions are inconsistent with security principle of least privilege (e.g., broad Bash allowances)
blockers.why_matters: Patterns like `Bash` (eval-running) or permissive `Bash(git *)` can still execute destructive or exfiltrating actions through allowed binaries/flags, expanding attack surface significantly.
blockers.location: Section 2.1: FR-1 allowed-tools table and tool restriction principles
blockers.recommendation: Replace broad Bash permissions with command+flag allowlists, add denylist for dangerous git/gh patterns, and enforce command parsing tests for each skill.

blockers.concern: Unknown compatibility with Claude Code agent hook API is a hard integration risk
blockers.why_matters: The design explicitly notes template syntax needs verification; if placeholders or response schema differ, FR-7 may not function at all and could block release sequencing.
blockers.location: Section 2.7: Known limitations (template syntax needs verification)
blockers.recommendation: Run a spike/prototype first to validate real hook contract (templating, JSON schema, timeout semantics) before full implementation commitments.
